Before reading the statement, read the questions. This may help you. Rockets are vehicles intended for transporting cargo and people to space. Depending on the amount of fuel used and the technology on board, they can reach the speed of 28000 km/h and put satellites into orbit around the Earth, as illustrated in the figure below. Such rockets are called orbital rockets. There are rockets whose apogee (maximum altitude reached by a rocket) is greater than 300 km, but the orbital speed of 28000 km/h is not reached. For this reason, they return to the Earth's surface, attracted by gravity. It is important to emphasize that the same force of gravity that brings suborbital rockets back to the Earth's surface is responsible for keeping satellites in their orbits. The fact that satellites do not fall like suborbital rockets is due to their speed of 28000 km/h, whose direction is parallel to the Earth's surface, as illustrated in the figure beside. Therefore, it is the combination of speed and gravity that keeps more than a thousand satellites operating in Earth orbit, at altitudes that vary from 300 km to 35800 km.

Although they cannot orbit the Earth, suborbital rockets are very useful for making measurements in the Earth's atmosphere and for testing new materials and devices that, in the future, may be applied to orbital rockets and satellites. Suborbital rockets are also used to carry out experiments in a microgravity environment, which allow the development of new materials and medicines. Microgravity is an environment in which the effects of the Earth's gravitational attraction are reduced, as a result of free-fall motion. In suborbital flights this condition is observed at altitudes above 100 km, provided that gravity is the only force acting on the rocket.

The Institute of Aeronautics and Space (IAE), located in the city of São José dos Campos, SP, develops a family of rockets, such as: VS-30, VSB-30 and VS-40. Since the Soviet Union put the satellite Sputnik in orbit, in 1957, almost six thousand satellites have been launched into space. On average two satellites are put into orbit per week. Among the applications of these satellites, it is worth highlighting: Communications, Meteorology, Earth Observation, Data Transmission and the Global Positioning System, the latter known in the western world by the acronym GPS.

There are currently about 450 Communications satellites in operation, some of which serve Brazilian territory. Although such satellites revolve around the Earth like all other satellites, they have characteristics of their own. One of them is that they take 24 hours to complete one turn around the Earth (this time is normally called the Orbital Period) in almost circular orbits. Since our planet also takes 24 hours to complete one rotation about its axis, everything happens as if the satellites were stationary ("parked") relative to a fixed point on the Earth's surface, as illustrated in the figure below. For this reason, they are also called geostationary. For this to be possible, such satellites need to be located in the plane of the terrestrial Equator at a specific distance from the Earth's surface. The table shows several orbital radii (distance measured between the satellite and the centre of the Earth) and respective orbital periods (the time needed, in hours, to make one turn around our planet).

Currently the geostationary satellites that serve Brazil belong to foreign companies. The Brazilian Government is about to acquire on the international market a communications satellite, the Geostationary Defence and Strategic Communications Satellite (SGDC). This satellite will offer the Brazilian population of areas lacking digital communication, normally that living in cities far from large urban centres, fast and cheap access to communications, including broadband Internet access via satellite. This satellite will also meet the needs of government, such as military communications.

problems.problem:
As you know, there are several ways of polluting the environment, among them, for example, the pollution of rivers, lakes, streets, land, atmosphere, etc. But there is also light pollution, which affects the beauty of the sky.

Question 10a) (0.5 point) (0.1 for each correct answer) Write TRUE or FALSE in front of each statement.

........ Lighting the sky harms the work of astronomers.
........ By lighting the sky we can see the Moon and the planets better.
........ By lighting the atmosphere we are wasting money and energy.
........ Public lighting should only light the ground and not the sky.
........ Lighting the atmosphere helps to see meteors!

Question 10b) (0.5 point) A 4 W lamp has been lit in the United States for 110 years, practically without ever having been switched off. It is a record that is already part of the Guinness Book, and brings many tourists to the city of Livermore, in California. The lamp was lit in 1901 and was turned off only for some power cuts and because of the change of the fire station building in 1976. It is an ordinary lamp, with the peculiarity of having a carbon filament (today's incandescent lamps use a tungsten filament). Manufactured at the end of 1890 by the Shelby Electric Company, a company that closed its doors in 1914, the lamp is so old that it was produced only eleven years after Thomas Edison made the first public demonstration of his invention. How much would its bill be, in reais, accumulated in the first century in which it was on, at the constant price of R\$0.20 per kWh? Consider all years equal to 365 days of 24 hours and ignore the few minutes in which it was off. Given: 1 kWh = 1000 (J/s) x 3600 s = 3600000 J. Hint: Simplify fractions before doing products.

Pergunta 10a) (0,5 ponto) (0,1 cada acerto) Escreva CERTO ou ERRADO na frente de cada afirmação.

Pergunta 10b) (0,5 ponto) Uma lâmpada de 4 W está acesa nos Estados Unidos há 110 anos, praticamente sem nunca ter sido desligada. É um recorde que já faz parte do Livro do Guiness, e leva muitos turistas à cidade de Livermore, na Califórnia. A lâmpada foi acesa em 1901 e foi apagada apenas por alguns cortes de energia e por causa da mudança de prédio dos bombeiros em 1976. Ela é uma lâmpada comum, com a particularidade de ter um filamento de carbono (as lâmpadas incandescentes de hoje usam filamento de tungstênio). Fabricada no final de 1890 pela Shelby Electric Company, empresa que fechou suas portas em 1914, a lâmpada é tão antiga que foi produzida apenas onze anos depois de Thomas Edison ter feito a primeira demonstração pública de sua invenção. Quanto seria sua conta, em reais, acumulada no primeiro século em que ela ficou ligada, ao preço constante de R\$0,20 por kWh? Considere todos os anos iguais a 365 dias de 24 horas e ignore os poucos minutos em que ela esteve apagada. Dado: 1 kWh = 1000 (J/s) x 3600 s = 3.600.000 J. problems.problem:
In the XVI OBA we showed how Eratosthenes measured the radius of the Earth. In this question we will show how you yourself can measure the diameter ($D$) of the Sun, knowing its distance to the Earth.

The first figure shows, schematically, the experiment. Make a tube with black cardboard, about 10 or 15 cm in diameter and as long as possible, like 1 or 2 metres. On one side cover it with aluminium foil and in its centre make a tiny hole with the tip of a fine needle. Cover the other side of the tube with a sheet of graph (millimetre) paper. In the first figure the tube is represented by a box. It does not matter. It can be a tube, a box or a parallelepiped. Since vertically opposite angles are equal, you can redraw the two light rays as in the diagram beside and use simple similarity of triangles to calculate the diameter of the Sun.

Question 1) By pointing the tube at the Sun, it projects its image on the graph paper, which can be measured. Bruna Senra, a student of UERJ, did this experiment with a tube 2 m long, 10 cm in diameter and the image of the Sun that she measured was 18 mm. Call $D$ the diameter of the Sun and $d$ the diameter of the image projected by the Sun on the graph paper (measured in the experiment). Call $T$ the Earth-Sun distance ($T = 150000000$ km) and $t$ the length of the tube. Calculate in km the value found by Bruna for the diameter, $D$, of the Sun. Hint: you only need a rule of three. Space for your calculations. A result without calculations will have no value at all!

problems.problem:
An important function of the telescope is to allow us to see separated astronomical bodies that with the naked eye we would see as only one, because they are very distant. For example, if you make two little black dots on a sheet of paper, separated by 1 cm from each other, you can see them separated if you move away to, approximately, 10 m. However the Hubble space telescope could see them separated even if they were 12 km away! We call angular resolution ($\phi$) the smallest angular separation at which our eye or the telescope can see two bodies or objects separated.

In a practical way, the angular resolution ($\phi$) (in seconds of arc), is calculated by the simplified formula $\phi = 200000\,\lambda / D$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of the light and $D$ the diameter of the mirror of the telescope or of the pupil of the eye. Both must be given in the same unit of length.

Question 7a) (0.4 point) Determine the angular resolution, in seconds of arc, of the human eye, knowing that the diameter of the pupil is about 4 mm and that we are sensitive to visible light, whose mean wavelength is $5 \times 10^{-4}$ mm.

Question 7b) (0.4 point) On a night with a clear sky and a Full Moon, an astronomy student wants to observe the crater Copernicus with the naked eye. Seen from the Earth, the angular diameter of the crater Copernicus is about 0.82 minutes of arc. Based on the calculation of the previous item, explain why the student can or cannot observe it. Given: 1 degree of arc = 60 minutes of arc and 1 minute of arc = 60 seconds of arc

Question 7c) (0.2 point) Determine the diameter $D$, in metres, of the primary mirror of the Hubble space telescope, knowing that for visible light, with mean wavelength of $5 \times 10^{-4}$ mm, its angular resolution is about 0.04 seconds of arc!
problems.problem_orig:
Uma importante função do telescópio é permitir ver separados astros que a olho nu veríamos como sendo um só, porque estão muito distantes. Por exemplo, se você fizer dois pontinhos pretos numa folha de papel, separados 1 cm um do outro, poderá vê-los separados se se afastar até, aproximadamente, 10 m. Contudo o telescópio espacial Hubble poderia vê-los separados mesmo que estivessem a 12 km! Chamamos de resolução angular ($\phi$) a menor separação angular que nosso olho ou o telescópio podem ver separados dois astros ou objetos.

De forma prática, a resolução angular ($\phi$) (em segundos de arco), é calculada pela fórmula simplificada $\phi = 200.000\,\lambda / D$, onde $\lambda$ é o comprimento de onda da luz e $D$ o diâmetro do espelho do telescópio ou da pupila do olho. Ambos devem ser dados na mesma unidade de comprimento.

Pergunta 7a) (0,4 ponto) Determine a resolução angular, em segundos de arco, do olho humano, sabendo que o diâmetro da pupila é de cerca de 4 mm e que somos sensíveis a luz visível, cujo comprimento de onda médio vale $5 \times 10^{-4}$ mm.

Pergunta 7b) (0,4 ponto) Em uma noite de céu limpo e Lua Cheia, um estudante de astronomia deseja observar a cratera Copérnico a olho nu. Vista da Terra, o diâmetro angular da cratera Copérnico é cerca de 0,82 minutos de arco. Baseado no cálculo do item anterior, explique por que o aluno pode ou não observá-la. Dado: 1 grau de arco = 60 minutos de arco e 1 minuto de arco = 60 segundos de arco

Pergunta 7c) (0,2 ponto) Determine o diâmetro $D$, em metros, do espelho primário do telescópio espacial Hubble, sabendo que para a luz visível, com comprimento de onda médio de $5 \times 10^{-4}$ mm, sua resolução angular é cerca 0,04 segundos de arco!

problems.problem:
The Institute of Aeronautics and Space (IAE) is the most important organization that designs and develops rockets in Brazil. The figure beside shows the typical flight of the VS-40 rocket, made up of the rocket motor and the payload. The rocket motor carries the propellant (= fuel + oxidizer) that drives the payload towards space. When the propellant is finished the structure of the rocket motor is separated from the payload, falling into the sea. By the speed acquired the payload (where the experiments are carried) continues its upward motion, now only under the action of the weight force and air resistance, until it reaches the point of maximum altitude, called the apogee. After the apogee the payload returns to the Earth's surface. While it flies above 100 km there is no longer propulsive force or air resistance. Under these conditions, any loose object inside it floats (microgravity environment). To reduce the speed of impact with the water, the recovery system (parachutes) is activated. After falling into the sea the payload is rescued by a helicopter and taken to a support point. The distance between the launch point and the impact point of the payload is called the range.

The angle formed between the axis of the rocket and the Earth's surface is called the elevation. If the elevation is 90 degrees the rocket is launched vertically, which never happens because parts of the rocket could fall on the launch site. Typically the elevation varies from 80 to 85 degrees. Another important definition is the azimuth, defined as the angle (measured clockwise) formed between the North direction and the direction of the launch of the rocket, as shown in the figure below. Taking the Barreira do Inferno Launch Centre (CLBI) as reference (see figure below), an azimuth of 0 degrees would mean launching the rocket towards the North, while an azimuth of 180 degrees would mean launching it towards the South. In practice the elevation and the azimuth are determined by the characteristics of the rocket to be launched, by the direction and intensity of the wind at the moment of launch, by the distance (range) desired for the payload, by the flight endurance of the helicopter and, for safety reasons, which aim to prevent the rocket from flying over inhabited regions. As shown in the table below, the elevation and the azimuth have a strong influence on the flight of the rocket and on the possibility of recovering the payload.

Option; Elevation (degrees); Azimuth (degrees); Range (km); Apogee (km); Flight time (s); Time above 100 km (s); Helicopter take-off point; Maximum flight distance of the helicopter (km)
1; 82; 330; 260; 200; 495; 300; A; 184
2; 80; 55; 298; 189; 485; 290; B; 280
3; 84; 120; 213; 213; 510; 316; C; 390

Question 8a) (0.25 point): If the microgravity time were the only determining factor for the choice of the elevation and the azimuth, which of the options shown in the table offers the longest microgravity time? Attention: An answer without a correct justification will have no value!

Question 8b) (0.25 point) Considering that a certain experiment needs at least 5 minutes in a microgravity environment, which of the 3 flight options would you choose, remembering that for the purposes of your analyses any part of the territory must be considered an inhabited region. Besides using the table, you must use the figure that illustrates the 3 different possible trajectories and justify your answer. Question 8c) (0.5 point) The impact point of the payload in the sea is an estimate that may vary as a function of the performance of the rocket motor, the aerodynamics of the vehicle and atmospheric conditions, mainly the intensity and direction of the wind at the various altitudes. For this reason, a region (and not a point) of impact is defined. This region is represented in the figure by a circle with a radius of 60 km. The payload may fall at any point inside the circle. In this way, the two helicopters of the Brazilian Air Force can only enter this circle after the payload has fallen into the sea. Besides emitting their position through the GPS system, the payload has a beacon that emits coloured smoke, thus making it easier to locate. One of the helicopters carries the SAR/IAE (Search and Rescue Support Service) team. Once the payload is located two frogmen dive into the sea and attach the steel cable of one of the helicopters to the payload, and the other helicopter rescues the frogmen. The flight time of the helicopters is limited by the amount of fuel they can carry. Moreover, after the rescue of the payload the speed developed by the helicopter is quite limited by the fact that the payload hangs from it. To define the azimuth the IAE team needs to define a support point for the SAR helicopters, represented as Point A, Point B and Point C in the figure. In your calculations, consider that, on average, the helicopter travels at 80 km/h and neglect the time for the helicopter to climb and descend, as well as the time to attach the payload to the helicopter. In the last column of the table are indicated the maximum distances that the helicopters will be able to travel to recover the payload, distances (outward and return) measured from Point A, Point B and Point C, respectively. In any of the situations the maximum flight time of the helicopter is 4 hours. Therefore, between its take-off and its return the maximum flight time is limited to four hours. problems.problem_orig:
O Instituto de Aeronáutica e Espaço (IAE) é a mais importante organização que projeta e desenvolve foguetes no Brasil. A figura ao lado mostra o voo típico do foguete VS-40, formado pelo motor-foguete e pela carga útil. O motor-foguete transporta o propelente (= combustível + oxidante) que impulsiona a carga útil rumo ao espaço. Terminado o propelente a estrutura do motor-foguete é separada da carga útil, caindo no mar. Pela velocidade adquirida a carga útil (onde são transportados os experimentos) continua o seu movimento ascendente, agora só sob ação da força peso e da resistência do ar, até atingir o ponto de altitude máxima, denominada apogeu. Após o apogeu a carga útil retorna à superfície terrestre. Enquanto voa acima dos 100 km não há mais a força propulsiva nem a resistência do ar. Nessas condições, qualquer objeto solto no seu interior flutua (ambiente de microgravidade). Para reduzir a velocidade de impacto com a água, o sistema de recuperação (paraquedas) é acionado. Após cair no mar a carga útil é resgatada por um helicóptero e levada a um ponto de apoio. A distância entre o ponto de lançamento e o ponto de impacto da carga útil denomina-se alcance.

O ângulo formado entre o eixo do foguete e a superfície terrestre chama-se elevação. Se a elevação for de 90 graus o foguete é lançado na vertical, o que nunca acontece porque partes do foguete poderiam cair sobre o local de lançamento. Tipicamente a elevação varia de 80 a 85 graus. Outra importante definição é o azimute, definido como o ângulo (medido no sentido horário) formado entre a direção Norte e a direção do lançamento do foguete, conforme mostrado na figura abaixo. Tomando o Centro de Lançamento da Barreira do Inferno (CLBI) como referência (vide figura abaixo), um azimute de 0 grau significaria lançar o foguete em direção ao Norte, enquanto um azimute de 180 graus significaria lançá-lo na direção Sul. Na prática a elevação e o azimute são determinados pelas características do foguete a ser lançado, pela direção e intensidade do vento no momento do lançamento, pela distância (alcance) desejada para a carga útil, pela autonomia de voo do helicóptero e, por condições de segurança, que objetivam impedir que o foguete sobrevoe regiões habitadas. Conforme mostrado na tabela abaixo, a elevação e o azimute têm forte influência sobre o voo do foguete e sobre a possibilidade de recuperação da carga útil.

Pergunta 8a) (0,25 ponto): Se o tempo de microgravidade fosse o único fator determinante para a escolha da elevação e do azimute, qual das opções mostradas na tabela oferece o maior tempo de microgravidade? Atenção: Resposta sem justificativa correta não terá valor!

Pergunta 8b) (0,25 ponto) Considerando que um determinado experimento necessite de pelo menos 5 minutos em ambiente de microgravidade, qual das 3 opções de voo você escolheria, lembrando que para efeitos de suas análises qualquer parte do território deve ser considerada região habitada. Além de fazer uso da tabela, você deverá usar a figura que ilustra as 3 diferentes trajetórias possíveis e justificar sua resposta. Atenção: Resposta sem justificativa correta não terá valor!

Pergunta 8c) (0,5 ponto) O ponto de impacto da carga útil no mar é uma estimativa que pode variar em função do desempenho do motor-foguete, da aerodinâmica do veículo e das condições atmosféricas, principalmente a intensidade e direção do vento nas várias altitudes. Por isso, é definida uma região (e não um ponto) de impacto. Essa região é representada na figura por uma circunferência com 60 km de raio. A carga útil pode cair em qualquer ponto do interior da circunferência. Dessa forma, os dois helicópteros da Força Aérea Brasileira somente podem ingressar nesse círculo depois que a carga útil cair no mar. Além de emitirem sua posição por meio do sistema GPS, a carga útil possui um sinalizador que emite uma fumaça colorida, facilitando, assim, a sua localização. Um dos helicópteros transporta a equipe do SAR/IAE (Serviço de Apoio e Resgate). Localizada a carga útil dois homens-rãs mergulham no mar e acoplam o cabo de aço de um dos helicópteros à carga útil, cabendo ao outro helicóptero resgatar os homens-rãs. O tempo de voo dos helicópteros é limitado pela quantidade de combustível que eles conseguem transportar. Além disso, após o resgate da carga útil a velocidade desenvolvida pelo helicóptero é bastante limitada pelo fato de a carga útil ficar pendurada a ele. Para definição do azimute a equipe do IAE precisa definir um ponto de apoio para os helicópteros do SAR, representados como Ponto A, Ponto B e Ponto C na figura. Nos seus cálculos, considere que, na média, o helicóptero se desloca a 80 km/h e despreze o tempo de subida e descida do helicóptero, bem como o tempo de fixação da carga útil ao helicóptero. Na última coluna da tabela estão indicadas as distâncias máximas que os helicópteros poderão percorrer para recuperar a carga útil, distâncias (ida e volta) essas medidas a partir do Ponto A, Ponto B e Ponto C, respectivamente. Em quaisquer das situações o tempo de voo máximo do helicóptero é de 4 horas. Portanto, entre a sua decolagem e o seu retorno o tempo máximo de voo é limitado a quatro horas. Considerando-se essas restrições, bem como outras já estabelecidas ao longo desta questão, determine quais das três opções de voo oferecidas é possível de ser realizada, ou em outras palavras, qual será o azimute desse voo. Atenção: Resposta sem justificativa correta não terá valor!

problems.problem:
Artificial satellites are made to revolve around the Earth with the most diverse objectives, among which it is worth highlighting: Communications, Meteorology, Earth Observation, Data Transmission and the Global Positioning System, the latter known in the western world by the acronym GPS. The mean distance of satellites to the Earth's surface varies according to the desired application. For example, if the objective of the satellite is to obtain detailed images of the Earth's surface the satellite is placed in an orbit whose mean distance from the Earth's surface varies between 700 and 900 km, this type of satellite having a mean speed of 27000 km/h. If the objective, however, is to use the satellite for Communications, the orbit used is the geostationary one. In this orbit the satellite is placed in the plane of the Equator at 35800 km distance from the Earth's surface. The satellites of the GPS system, in turn, are situated about 20200 km from the Earth's surface, moving at a mean speed of 14040 km/h.

In principle, Kepler's laws are also applicable to satellites. These laws are valid when the Earth is assumed to be spherical and with uniform mass distribution and no other force acting on the satellite. In the real world, these hypotheses do not apply, because besides the non-sphericity of the Earth, the Sun, the Moon and solar radiation, among other factors, act on the satellite altering its Keplerian orbit.

Question 9a) (0.25 point) Considering the radius of the Earth to be 6376 km, calculate in km/h the mean speed of a geostationary satellite, considering that it completes one turn around the Earth every 24 hours. In your calculations use $\pi = 3$. Attention! Your answer will only be accepted if your calculations are recorded here.

Question 9b) (0.25 point) A satellite in geostationary orbit completes one turn around the Earth every 24 hours. If it is positioned over the plane of the Equator and at 35800 km from the Earth's surface, the satellite will stay "stationary" relative to a fixed point on the Earth, thus making it easier to emit and receive signals between the satellite and the transmitting station located on the Earth. As already mentioned, the satellite is continuously pulled out of its ideal operating position, which is why it needs to be constantly repositioned by means of orbital manoeuvres. To carry out these manoeuvres the satellite intermittently fires several thrusters that use propellant (fuel + oxidizer) stored in the satellite. Currently it is the amount of propellant that limits the life of a geostationary satellite. Considering that a satellite has a total mass of 5000 kg, of which 2400 kg is propellant, what percentage of the mass of the satellite is propellant? Attention! Your answer will only be accepted if your calculations are recorded here.

Question 9c) (0.5 point) If this geostationary satellite uses 20 kg of propellant per month to stay in the desired geostationary orbit, what will its useful life be in years, considering that 2% of the propellant mass of the satellite must be reserved to carry out the final manoeuvre of its useful life, which consists of taking it out of the 35800 km orbit and taking it to a "graveyard" orbit, located above 36000 km? From this last manoeuvre the satellite will become space debris and will allow a new satellite to be placed in the orbital position previously occupied by it. Attention! Your answer will only be accepted if your calculations are recorded here.
problems.problem_orig:
Satélites artificiais são feitos para girarem em torno da Terra com os mais diversos objetivos, dentre os quais vale destacar: Comunicações, Meteorologia, Observação da Terra, Transmissão de Dados e Sistema de Posicionamento Global, esta última conhecida no mundo ocidental pela sigla GPS. A distância média dos satélites à superfície terrestre varia de acordo com a aplicação desejada. Por exemplo, se o objetivo do satélite é obter imagens detalhadas da superfície terrestre o satélite é posicionado numa órbita, cuja distância média da superfície da Terra varia entre 700 e 900 km, possuindo esse tipo de satélite uma velocidade média de 27.000 km/h. Se o objetivo, entretanto, for utilizar o satélite para Comunicações, a órbita utilizada é a geoestacionária. Nessa órbita o satélite é colocado no plano do Equador a 35.800 km de distância da superfície terrestre. Já os satélites do sistema GPS, situam-se a cerca de 20.200 km de distância da superfície terrestre, movendo-se numa velocidade média de 14.040 km/h.

Em princípio, aos satélites também são aplicáveis as leis de Kepler. Essas leis são válidas quando a Terra é assumida como sendo esférica e com distribuição uniforme de massa e nenhuma outra força atuando no satélite. No mundo real, essas hipóteses não são aplicáveis, pois além da não esfericidade da Terra, o Sol, a Lua e a radiação solar, dentre outros fatores, atuam sobre o satélite alterando sua órbita kepleriana.

Pergunta 9a) (0,25 ponto) Considerando o raio da Terra como sendo de 6.376 km, calcule em km/h a velocidade média de um satélite geoestacionário, considerando que ele completa uma volta em torno da Terra a cada 24 horas. Nos seus cálculos use $\pi = 3$. Atenção! Sua resposta só será aceita se tiver suas contas registradas aqui.

Pergunta 9b) (0,25 ponto) Um satélite em órbita geoestacionária completa um giro em torno da Terra a cada 24 horas. Se ele estiver posicionado sobre o plano do Equador e a 35.800 km da superfície da Terra, o satélite ficará “parado” em relação a um ponto fixo na Terra, facilitando, assim, a emissão e recepção de sinais entre o satélite e a estação transmissora localizada na Terra. Como já mencionado, o satélite é continuamente tirado da sua posição ideal de operação, razão pela qual ele precisa ser constantemente reposicionado por meio de manobras orbitais. Para executar essas manobras o satélite aciona de modo intermitente vários propulsores que utilizam propelente (combustível + oxidante) armazenado no satélite. Atualmente é a quantidade de propelente que limita a vida de um satélite geoestacionário. Considerando-se que um satélite possua uma massa total de 5.000 kg, sendo 2.400 kg de propelente, qual o percentual da massa do satélite é propelente? Atenção! Sua resposta só será aceita se tiver suas contas registradas aqui.

Pergunta 9c) (0,5 ponto) Se esse satélite geoestacionário fizer uso de 20 kg de propelente por mês para se manter na órbita geoestacionária desejada, qual será sua vida útil em anos, considerando que 2% da massa de propelente do satélite deve ser reservada para realizar a manobra final da sua vida útil, que consiste em tirá-lo da órbita de 35.800 km e levá-lo para uma órbita “cemitério”, localizada acima dos 36.000 km? A partir dessa última manobra o satélite tornar-se-á lixo espacial e permitirá que um novo satélite seja colocado na posição orbital anteriormente ocupada por ele. Atenção! Sua resposta só será aceita se tiver suas contas registradas aqui.

problems.problem:
Fires occur for natural reasons (through lightning, for example) or anthropic ones (caused by humans). However, about 90% of fires are of anthropic origin. Fires contribute to the accumulation of carbon dioxide (CO$_2$) and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, thus affecting not only local and regional air quality, but also the global climate. As a result of the deforestation of the Amazon Forest and of agricultural practices that use fire to clear the surface, Brazil is considered the country that emits the most greenhouse gases.

Sensors installed on artificial satellites make it possible to identify regions of the Earth's surface where fires occur. These sensors work based on the principle of Planck's Law, which establishes that the emission of electromagnetic energy depends on the temperature of the body and on the wavelength. As illustrated in the Figure, the Sun, with a mean surface temperature close to 5762 K, emits the greatest intensity of its radiation in the wavelength range of visible light ($0.4$ to $0.7 \times 10^{-6}\,\mu$m), while the Earth, with a mean surface temperature close to 288 K ($\approx 15\,^\circ$C) emits most of its radiation in the infrared wavelength range (wavelengths above 0.7 $\mu$m, where $1\,\mu\mathrm{m} = 10^{-6}$ m). The Figure also shows that the higher the temperature, the greater the maximum intensity of radiation emitted, observing also that the point of maximum intensity moves to the left as the temperature is raised.

Question 10a) (0.5 point) The relation between temperature ($T$) and wavelength ($\lambda$), at which the maximum of the energy emitted by a body is observed, is given by Wien's displacement law:

$$\lambda \times T_{\text{max}} = 2898\ \mu\mathrm{m\,K}.$$

Thus, for the temperature of 288 K, the maximum intensity occurs at 10 $\mu$m, while at 5672 K, it occurs at 0.5 $\mu$m, within the visible range, known as light and to which our eyes are most sensitive. Considering that the mean surface temperature of fires is 1200 K, at which wavelength should the satellite sensor be calibrated to best detect the existence of fires? Attention! Your answer will only be accepted if your calculations are recorded here.

Question 10b) (0.5 point) In a simplified way, the total amount of energy (considering all wavelengths) emitted by an object is given by the Stefan-Boltzmann Law: $E = \sigma T^4$, where $\sigma = 5.67 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}K^{-4}}$ and $T$ is the surface temperature of the object given on the Kelvin scale. Considering that the typical temperature of a fire is 1200 K (four times the mean temperature of the Earth's surface), how many times more energy does a fire emit when compared with the emission of the Earth's surface? Attention! Your answer will only be accepted if your calculations are recorded here.

As queimadas ocorrem por motivos naturais (através de raios, por exemplo) ou antrópicos (provocadas pelos homens). No entanto, cerca de 90% das queimadas são de origem antrópica. As queimadas contribuem para o acúmulo de dióxido de carbono (CO$_2$) e outros gases do efeito estufa na atmosfera, afetando, desta forma, não somente a qualidade do ar local e regional, mas também o clima global. Em decorrência do desmatamento da Floresta Amazônica e de práticas agrícolas que utilizam a queimada para limpar a superfície, o Brasil é considerado o país que mais emite gases do efeito estufa.

Sensores instalados em satélites artificiais permitem identificar regiões da superfície terrestre onde ocorrem queimadas. Esses sensores funcionam baseados no princípio da Lei de Planck, que estabelece que a emissão de energia eletromagnética é dependente da temperatura do corpo e do comprimento de onda. Conforme ilustrado na Figura, o Sol, com uma temperatura média superficial próxima aos 5762 K emite a maior intensidade da sua radiação na faixa de comprimento de onda da luz visível ($0{,}4$ a $0{,}7 \times 10^{-6}\,\mu$m), enquanto a Terra, com uma temperatura superficial média próxima a 288 K ($\approx 15\,^\circ$C) emite a maior parte da sua radiação na faixa de comprimento do infravermelho (comprimentos de onda acima de 0,7 $\mu$m, onde $1\,\mu\mathrm{m} = 10^{-6}$ m). A Figura também mostra que quanto maior a temperatura, maior é a intensidade máxima de radiação emitida, observando-se, ainda que o ponto de máxima intensidade move-se para a esquerda, na medida em que a temperatura é elevada.

Pergunta 10a) (0,5 ponto) A relação entre temperatura ($T$) e comprimento de onda ($\lambda$), no qual se observa o máximo da energia emitida por um corpo, é dada pela Lei do deslocamento de Wien:

$$\lambda \times T_{\text{máxima}} = 2898\ \mu\mathrm{m\,K}.$$

Dessa forma, para a temperatura de 288 K, a intensidade máxima se dá a 10 $\mu$m, enquanto a 5672 K, ela ocorre a 0,5 $\mu$m, dentro da faixa do visível, conhecida como luz e na qual nossos olhos são mais sensíveis. Considerando que a temperatura média superficial das queimadas é de 1200 K, em qual comprimento de onda o sensor do satélite deve ser calibrado para melhor captar a existência de queimadas? Atenção! Sua resposta só será aceita se tiver suas contas registradas aqui.

Pergunta 10b) (0,5 ponto) De uma maneira simplificada, a quantidade de energia total (considerando todos os comprimentos de onda) emitida por um objeto é dada pela Lei de Stefan-Boltzmann: $E = \sigma T^4$, onde $\sigma = 5{,}67 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}K^{-4}}$ e $T$ é a temperatura superficial do objeto dada na escala Kelvin. Considerando que a temperatura típica de uma queimada é de 1200 K (quatro vezes a temperatura média da superfície terrestre), quantas vezes mais energia emite uma queimada quando comparada à emissão da superfície terrestre? Atenção! Sua resposta só será aceita se tiver suas contas registradas aqui.

problems.problem:
Observing the planet Venus daily, we see that it crosses the imaginary Earth-Sun line and moves away until a maximum value, which we call the greatest elongation. Then it apparently comes back to approach the Sun, passes behind the Sun, reappears and moves away from it until the same maximum separation already observed on the other side. The figure illustrates the maximum separation on one of the sides. Copernicus did not know the distance between the Earth and the Sun, so he called it $D = 1$ A.U. (one Astronomical Unit), but he knew elementary geometry, that is, he knew that:

$$\frac{h}{d} = \frac{H}{D}$$

problems.problem:
Rockets are used to take cargo or people to space. For simplicity, we will deal only with sending cargo to space and will represent the rocket as being composed of three parts: fairing, fins and rocket motor. The fairing is represented by a dark triangle, and is used to protect the cargo during the ascending flight in the Earth's atmosphere. The fins, located at the bottom of the rocket, are small "wings" used to give stability to the rocket during flight. However, more than 80% of the mass of a rocket is propellant (fuel and oxidizer). In general, the propellant is distributed in one or more motors, for reasons that will be explained below.

More than a century ago the Russian Konstantin Tsiolkovsky showed that the gain in velocity obtained by burning the propellant of each motor of a rocket is given by the famous equation known as the "rocket equation" (given beside)

$$\Delta v = \text{constant} \times \ln\left(m_i / m_f\right)$$

where "ln" is the Neperian logarithm function, or natural logarithm, whose values are given in the table beside for different values of $m_i / m_f$. For example, for $m_i / m_f = 9.0$, $\ln(m_i / m_f) = 2.2$.

$m_i / m_f$: 1.7, 2.4, 3.5, 5.0, 6.0, 9.0
$\ln(m_i / m_f)$: 0.5, 0.9, 1.3, 1.6, 1.8, 2.2

The constant that appears in the rocket equation varies with the type of propellant used and with the performance of the motor. To simplify we will use constant = 3000 m/s, where $m_i$ is the initial mass of the rocket and $m_f$ its final mass, obtained by subtracting the mass of propellant from the initial mass of the rocket. It is worth noting that the "rocket equation" does not consider gravitational and aerodynamic losses, which are of the order of 25%.

Question 8a) (0.25 point) A rocket with a single motor has an initial mass of 120000 kg, of which 100000 kg is propellant. Using the Tsiolkovsky equation and the given table, calculate the velocity that the rocket transfers to the payload. Below there is space for your calculations. Without them the result will have no value.

The gain in velocity obtained in the previous item is applied both to the payload, which has a mass of 500 kg, and to the (empty) propellant tank of the rocket, which by the values presented has a mass of 19500 kg! As a result, an engineer proposes to divide the propellant mass of this rocket into two motors. In ALTERNATIVE 1 the propellant is divided equally into two motors (stages), while in ALTERNATIVE 2, the first stage carries 80000 kg of propellant and the second 20000 kg. By applying the Tsiolkovsky equation to the flight of each of the stages and adding the results, it is possible to calculate the final velocity transferred to the payload, as presented in the table below, for the two alternatives proposed. The mass of the structure of the 1st stage is discarded before the 2nd stage starts.

Alternative 1; 1st Stage; 2nd Stage
propellant mass (kg); 50000; 50000
structure mass (kg); 10000; 9500
payload mass; -; 500
$m_i / m_f$; 1.7; 6
$\Delta v$ (m/s); 1617; 5375
Total $\Delta v$ (m/s) = 1617 + 5375 = 6992 m/s

Alternative 2; 1st Stage; 2nd Stage
propellant mass (kg); 80000; 20000
structure mass (kg); 16000; 3500
payload mass; -; 500
$m_i / m_f$; 3; 6
$\Delta v$; 3296; 5375
Total $\Delta v$ (m/s) = 3296 + 5375 = 8671 m/s

Question 8b) (0.25 point): The masses of propellant, structure and payload are the same in the 3 options evaluated. Copy your result of question 8a into the blank cell of the table beside. Put an X on the dashed line, under the alternative that, in your opinion, is the best option in terms of velocity gain of the payload.

$\Delta v$ Initial proposal: (blank); $\Delta v$ Alternative 1: 6992 m/s; $\Delta v$ Alternative 2: 8671 m/s

Question 8c) (0.5 point): Justify your answer to the previous question.

Foguetes são utilizados para levar cargas ou pessoas ao espaço. Por simplicidade, trataremos apenas do envio de cargas ao espaço e representaremos o foguete como sendo composto de três partes: coifa, empenas e motor-foguete. A coifa é representada por um triângulo escuro, sendo utilizada para proteger a carga durante o voo ascendente na atmosfera terrestre. As empenas, localizadas na parte inferior do foguete, são pequenas “asas” utilizadas para dar estabilidade ao foguete durante o voo. No entanto, mais de 80% da massa de um foguete é propelente (combustível e oxidante). Em geral, o propelente é distribuído em um ou mais motores, pelas razões que serão explicadas a seguir.

Há mais de um século o russo Konstantin Tsiolkovsky demonstrou que o ganho de velocidade obtido pela queima do propelente de cada motor de um foguete é dado pela famosa equação conhecida como “equação do foguete,” (dada ao lado)

$$\Delta v = \text{constante} \times \ln\left(m_i / m_f\right)$$

onde “ln” é a função logaritmo neperiano, ou logaritmo natural, cujos valores são dados na tabela ao lado para diferentes valores de $m_i / m_f$. Por exemplo, para $m_i / m_f = 9{,}0$, $\ln(m_i / m_f) = 2{,}2$.

$m_i / m_f$: 1,7; 2,4; 3,5; 5,0; 6,0; 9,0
$\ln(m_i / m_f)$: 0,5; 0,9; 1,3; 1,6; 1,8; 2,2

A constante que aparece na equação do foguete varia com o tipo de propelente utilizado e com o desempenho do motor. Para simplificar utilizaremos constante = 3.000 m/s, sendo que $m_i$ é a massa inicial do foguete e $m_f$ a sua massa final, obtida subtraindo-se a massa de propelente da massa inicial do foguete. Vale registrar que a “equação do foguete” não considera as perdas gravitacionais e aerodinâmicas, que são da ordem de 25%.

massa do propelente (kg); 50.000; 50.000
massa da estrutura (kg); 10.000; 9.500
massa da carga útil; -; 500
$m_i / m_f$; 1,7; 6
$\Delta v$ (m/s); 1.617; 5.375
$\Delta v$ total (m/s) = 1.617 + 5.375 = 6.992 m/s

Alternativa 2; 1º Estágio; 2º Estágio
massa do propelente (kg); 80.000; 20.000
massa da estrutura (kg); 16.000; 3.500
massa da carga útil; -; 500
$m_i / m_f$; 3; 6
$\Delta v$; 3.296; 5.375
$\Delta v$ total (m/s) = 3.296 + 5.375 = 8.671 m/s

Pergunta 8b) (0,25 ponto): A massa de propelente, de estrutura e da carga-útil são as mesmas nas 3 opções avaliadas. Copie seu resultado da pergunta 8a para a célula em branco da tabela ao lado. The Space Age was inaugurated on 4 October 1957, when the former Soviet Union put the satellite Sputnik in orbit around the Earth (see the figure beside). Since then, more than 7000 satellites have been launched into space, helping us with weather forecasting, monitoring of Amazon deforestation and broadcasting of great events such as the World Cup and the Olympic Games. Of the 1200 satellites currently in operation, 400 are intended for communications. Communications satellites follow circular orbits situated in the plane of the Equator at a distance such that they complete one turn around the Earth in 23h56min4s, that is, in the same period as the rotation of the Earth (if necessary, round this value to 24h). For all practical purposes, they stay "stationary" relative to a fixed point on the Earth situated on the Equator line, which is why they are called geostationary.

Question 9a) (0.25 point) Considering that, in each turn around the Earth, a geostationary satellite travels the distance of 265000 km, what is its mean speed in km/h? Do your calculations below. Without them the result will not be accepted.

Question 9b) (0.25 point) The Table below shows the speed for several circular orbits in the plane of the terrestrial Equator. Based on this table and on the result you obtained in Question 9a, put an X on the radius of the orbit of the geostationary satellite mentioned in question 9a.

Orbital radius (km): 6630; 6728; 7378; 16378; 42160
Orbital speed (km/h): 27926; 27718; 26469; 17765; 11042

Putting a satellite in orbit requires a great deal of knowledge, work, technology, specialized laboratories and financial resources. Besides the satellite, a rocket with enough energy to carry the satellite to space is needed. Normally, the mass of propellant (fuel + oxidizer) makes up 90% of the total mass of the rocket, the mass of the satellite being less than 1% of the total mass of the rocket.

Although the first artificial satellite of the Earth was launched in 1957, in 1925 the German engineer Dr. Walter Hohmann had already thought about the problem. Is it not incredible? Based on knowledge of orbital mechanics Hohmann proposed the theory that became known as the Hohmann transfer orbit, which minimizes the amount of energy (propellant) needed to put satellites and spacecraft in orbit around the Earth. Do not worry, we will explain Dr. Hohmann's brilliant idea to you.

In a simplified way, Dr. Hohmann's idea works as follows: instead of the rocket putting the geostationary satellite in its final orbit, represented by the solid line of the figure beside, it puts it at point B situated about 200 km from the Earth's surface. From point B the motion of the satellite will be subject to the laws of orbital mechanics and it will revolve anticlockwise along an elliptical orbit represented by the dashed line of the figure. For communication purposes, this satellite would not have any use since its position relative to a fixed point on the Earth's surface located on the terrestrial Equator changes with time. But this is where Hohmann's brilliant idea comes in. According to his theory, the geostationary orbit can be reached by firing the thruster of the satellite at the apogee of its elliptical trajectory (point C of the figure) and with this it will leave its elliptical orbit and reach the geostationary orbit.

Question 9c) (0.5 point) By the laws of orbital mechanics, each orbit, whether elliptical or circular, has a specific orbital energy, defined by $\varepsilon = v^2/2 - \mu/R$, where $v$ is the speed of the satellite, $R$ is the local radius of the orbit (measured from the centre of the Earth) and $\mu \approx 4 \times 10^5$ km$^3$/s$^2$. For the orbits shown in the figure we have ($\varepsilon_e =$) $\varepsilon_{\text{elliptical}} = -8.2$ km$^2$/s$^2$ and ($\varepsilon_c =$) $\varepsilon_{\text{circular}} = -4.7$ km$^2$/s$^2$. Calculate by how much ($\Delta v$) the speed of the satellite increased when it passed from the elliptical orbit to the circular one at point C. A Era Espacial foi inaugurada em 04 de outubro de 1957, quando a antiga União Soviética colocou o satélite Sputnik em órbita da Terra (vide figura ao lado). Desde então, mais de 7.000 satélites foram lançados ao espaço, nos auxiliando na previsão do tempo, monitoramento do desmatamento da Amazônia e transmissão de grandes eventos como Copa do Mundo e Olimpíadas. Dos 1.200 satélites em operação atualmente, 400 são destinados às comunicações. Os satélites de comunicações percorrem órbitas circulares situadas no plano do Equador a uma distância tal que completam uma volta em torno da Terra em 23h56min4seg, ou seja, no mesmo período de rotação da Terra (se necessário, aproxime este valor para 24h). Para todos os efeitos práticos, eles ficam “parados” em relação a um ponto fixo da Terra situado na linha do Equador, razão pela qual são chamados geoestacionários.

Pergunta 9a) (0,25 ponto) Considerando-se que, em cada volta em torno da Terra, um satélite geoestacionário percorre a distância de 265.000 km, qual a sua velocidade média em km/h? Faça abaixo suas contas. Sem elas o resultado não será aceito.

Colocar um satélite em órbita exige muito conhecimento, trabalho, tecnologia, laboratórios especializados e recursos financeiros. Além do satélite, é preciso um foguete com energia suficiente para transportar o satélite ao espaço. Normalmente, a massa de propelente (combustível + oxidante) constitui 90% da massa total do foguete, sendo a massa do satélite inferior a 1% da massa total do foguete.

Embora o primeiro satélite artificial da Terra tenha sido lançado em 1957, em 1925 o engenheiro alemão Dr. Walter Hohmann já tinha pensado no problema. Não é incrível? Baseado no conhecimento da mecânica orbital Hohmann propôs a teoria que ficou conhecida como órbita de transferência de Hohmann, que minimiza a quantidade de energia (propelente) necessária para colocar satélites e espaçonaves em órbita da Terra. Fique tranquilo, que vamos lhe explicar a genial ideia do Dr. Hohmann.

De uma maneira simplificada, a ideia do Dr. Hohmann funciona da seguinte forma: em vez do foguete colocar o satélite geoestacionário em sua órbita final, representada pela linha cheia da figura ao lado, ele o coloca no ponto B situado a cerca de 200 km de distância da superfície terrestre. A partir do ponto B o movimento do satélite estará sujeito às leis da mecânica orbital e girará no sentido anti-horário ao longo de uma órbita elíptica representada pela linha tracejada da figura. Para efeitos de comunicação, este satélite não teria qualquer utilidade uma vez que a sua posição em relação a um ponto fixo da superfície terrestre localizado no Equador terrestre muda com o tempo. Mas é aqui que entra a genial ideia de Hohmann. De acordo com sua teoria, a órbita geoestacionária pode ser alcançada acionando o propulsor do satélite no apogeu de sua trajetória elíptica (ponto C da figura) e com isso ele sairá de sua órbita elíptica e alcançará a órbita geoestacionária.

In the last 300 years man has destroyed at least 50% of all the forests of the planet. In Brazil, the Legal Amazon includes the states of Amazonas, Acre, Pará, Amapá, Roraima, Rondônia, Mato Grosso, Maranhão, Goiás and Tocantins, has 5 million square kilometres and represents 61% of the national territory. The deforestation of the Amazon forest has already reached more than 13%, generating consequences such as loss of biodiversity, soil degradation and changes in the climate, which altered the rainfall and wind regime in the Legal Amazon and in the centre-west and south-east regions of the country.

Images obtained by remote sensing satellites, such as CBERS-4, developed jointly by Brazil and China, make it possible to monitor and measure the felling of the forest. The precision of this measurement depends on the spatial resolution of the satellite sensors. The resolution of the satellite sensors can be compared to the acuity of human eyes, that is, some satellites see better than others. The sensors of the American Landsat series satellites, for example, have a spatial resolution of 30 metres. This means that objects separated from each other by less than 30 metres will not, in general, be discriminated by the sensor. The MODIS sensors aboard the Terra and Aqua satellites, in turn, produce images of the Earth's surface with resolutions of 250, 500 and 1000 metres.

Question 10a) (0.5 point) Remote sensing satellites revolve around the Earth in an orbit whose plane passes close to the Earth's poles. The relative motion of these satellites with respect to the Earth is such that they image the whole globe in a time interval of 26 days. In a simplified way it can be stated that every month a remote sensing satellite obtains the "portrait" of the whole Legal Amazon. By comparing the "portrait" of one month with that of the previous month, the specialists of the National Institute for Space Research (INPE) can monitor the increase of the deforested area, as well as identify new deforested areas, thus informing the competent authorities of the location of these areas. These authorities can then go to the indicated places and identify those responsible. Based on these explanations, which, among the 4 spatial resolutions mentioned in this question, would be the most suitable for this service? Justify your answer.

Question 10b) (0.5 point) When intending to examine a deforested area of 10000 m$^2$, which resolution would be the most suitable for this study? Justify your answer.

problems.problem:
The year 2016 is a Leap Year! Our calendar is based on the Tropical Year. This is the time that the Sun, in its apparent annual motion, takes between being at the zenith at the Tropic of Capricorn, going to and being at the zenith at the Tropic of Cancer and returning to be at the zenith at the Tropic of Capricorn. When the Sun is at the zenith at the Tropic of Capricorn or of Cancer, we say that the Summer Solstice is occurring in that Hemisphere. To go from one Tropic to the other, it passes at the zenith through the Celestial Equator and when this occurs we say that the Equinox is occurring.

That is why we call it the Tropical Year, since the Sun oscillates between the two Tropics. The duration of this Tropical Year is approximately 365.25 days. Its advantage is that the seasons of the year always begin approximately on the same dates, besides the simple observation of the Equinoxes and Solstices.

Below we show a schematic figure illustrating this oscillation of the Sun in its apparent annual motion between the tropics, supposing the Earth motionless, of course.

Schematic figure of the oscillation of the Sun between the two tropics. In this figure HN and HS mean Northern and Southern Hemisphere, respectively. This "oscillation" of the Sun only occurs because of the tilt of the Earth's rotation axis relative to the perpendicular to the plane of its orbit. If the rotation axis were perpendicular to the plane of the orbit none of this would happen and there would be no seasons of the year.

problems.problem:
In Astronomy we often need to measure the angular separation of two bodies or the angular size of a body. Suppose that in the figure beside, $L$ is the diameter of the Sun, that is, about $1.4 \times 10^6$ km and $R$ its mean distance to the Earth, which is about $150 \times 10^6$ km. With this, the angular diameter subtended by the Sun, seen from the Earth, is, in radians:

$$\theta = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{1.4 \times 10^6\ \text{km}}{150 \times 10^6\ \text{km}} = \frac{1.4}{150} = 9.33 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{radian}.$$

In a circle we have 360$^\circ$ or $2\pi$ radians, so, by the "rule of three", we have that 1 radian is equivalent to about 60 degrees. Thus, the angular diameter of the Sun, seen from the Earth, is, in degrees:

$$\theta = 9.33 \times 10^{-3} \times 60\ \text{degrees} = 0.56\ \text{degree}.$$

Question 6a) (0.5 point) In the near future Mars will be colonized. What will be the angular diameter, in degrees, with which these colonizers will see the Sun? The mean Sun-Mars distance is about $228 \times 10^6$ km. Hint: Just repeat the calculation above. The result must be in degrees.

Rockets are vehicles developed to transport people or satellites to space. For this they make use of a large amount of propellant (fuel + oxidizer), which allows them to reach the speed of 27000 km/h. The propellant is divided into two tanks (stages). After the propellant has been consumed, the 1st stage is ejected and the engine of the 2nd stage is ignited, inserting the satellite into its orbit, as illustrated by the dashed line of the figure on the right. Because of its speed, the empty engine of the 2nd stage also stays in orbit, becoming space debris. Communications satellites cost one billion reais and have a useful life of 15 years. To put them in orbit, rockets are used whose launches cost 400 million reais.

Question 8a) (0.25 point) Rockets, like the one illustrated in the figure beside, have a height equivalent to a 20-storey building and a diameter of 4 metres. At launch they have a mass of 550000 kg, including 500000 kg of propellant and the 5500 kg of the satellite. What is the percentage of the mass of the satellite relative to the total mass of the rocket? Record your calculations below, without them the result is not accepted.

Question 8b) (0.25 point) In rockets developed until the end of the last century, the engine of the 1st stage, after being ejected, fell into the sea, and was not recovered. With the aim of reducing launch costs by 25%, a company proposes to recover the 1st stage of the rocket on the ground and reuse it. According to this proposal, after separating from the 2nd stage, the engine of the 1st stage performs the manoeuvre represented by the solid line shown in the figure above, and begins its descending motion towards the Earth's surface.

From the apogee, two forces act on the "empty" engine of the 1st stage: i) the force of gravity, which will make its speed increase by 10 m/s for each second of descent and ii) the drag force, resulting from the interaction between the engine of the 1st stage and the Earth's atmosphere (located below 100 km altitude). The friction between the engine and the atmosphere generates heat. The friction force is proportional to the square of the speed, while the heat is proportional to the cube of the speed. To prevent the engine from melting during atmospheric re-entry, it is proposed to fire the engines of the 1st stage during the descent for 20 seconds (Point 1 of the figure), making the speed reduce from 4500 km/h to 1000 km/h. At this speed, the drag force and the force of gravity balance each other, making the resulting acceleration zero. To prevent destruction of the engine on impact with the ground, this company proposes to fire the engines of the 1st stage once more (Point 2 of the figure), making the stage land gently on the ground. From the point of view of space engineering this proposal carries countless challenges, one of them being the use of more propellant, as you will calculate below. From the Rocket Equation, proposed more than a century ago by the Russian Konstantin Tsiolkovsky (1857-1935), the mass of propellant, $M_p$, needed to obtain a certain $\Delta v$ (in km/h) is given by $M_p = M_f\,(e^x - 1)$, where $M_f$ is the final mass of the engine after the propellant mass, $M_p$, has been consumed, and $e^x$ is the exponential function, whose values are presented in the Table.

Foguetes são veículos desenvolvidos para transportar pessoas ou satélites ao espaço. Para tanto, eles fazem uso de grande quantidade de propelente (combustível + oxidante), que lhes permite alcançar a velocidade de 27.000 km/h. O propelente é dividido em dois tanques (estágios). Em função de sua velocidade, o motor vazio do 2º estágio também fica em órbita, tornando-se lixo espacial. Satélites de comunicações custam um bilhão de reais e têm 15 anos de vida útil. In August and September 2016 thousands of athletes from all over the planet will take part in the Olympic and Paralympic Games in the city of Rio de Janeiro. It will be up to geostationary satellites to bring the images of the games to millions of citizens of Brazil and of the world. Geostationary satellites are located in the equatorial plane and revolve around the longitudinal axis of the Earth with the same angular velocity ($\omega$) as it, as illustrated in the figure beside. Everything happens as if the satellite stayed motionless relative to the Earth. Hence its name geostationary ("parked" relative to the Earth). From this privileged position, they act as mirrors that, on receiving the signals containing image and sound from the Maracanã, spread them over the whole Brazilian territory, where they can be picked up by antennas. For those countries on the other side of the globe, in Japan, for example, the signal path is longer and may involve up to 3 geostationary satellites.

The SGDC will be "parked" at a longitude of 75$^\circ$ West. From this position it will be able to cover the whole Brazilian territory and some more regions around it. problems.problem:
In a simplified way a remote sensing satellite can be understood as a "camera" that, from space, obtains images of the Earth. From these images it is possible to monitor and measure various phenomena that occur on the Earth's surface, including fires and deforestation. It is important to stress, however, that the identification of fires is made from the capture of the energy emitted by the organic material in flames, which occurs mainly in the wavelength range between 3.7 $\mu$m and 4.1 $\mu$m (1 $\mu$m = $10^{-6}$ m) of the electromagnetic spectrum, known as mid-thermal. It is known that the higher the temperature of the flame, the greater the emission of energy. Deforestation, in turn, is identified from the reflected solar radiation in a wavelength range between 0.4 $\mu$m and 3.0 $\mu$m. On analysing the solar radiation reflected by the types of surface at the various wavelengths of solar radiation it is observed that water (rivers, lakes and seas) reflects less solar energy when compared with soil without vegetation cover and with soil with vegetation cover. Moreover, exposed soil and vegetation reflect differently at all wavelengths, which allows their differentiation. Since these are distinct physical phenomena (emission and reflection) the satellite needs to have more than one imaging camera to monitor deforestation and fires.

Similarly to a digital camera, the images obtained by the sensors of a satellite are transformed into pixels. Each image is composed of millions of pixels. The pixel is the smallest element of the image, to which it is possible to assign a tone, whose numerical value varies between zero and 255. A pixel with value zero means that it received almost no radiation coming from the Earth's surface, being then represented by the colour black. At the other extreme the value 255 corresponds to the colour white and indicates that the sensor received the maximum amount of radiation from the Earth's surface. Between zero and 255 there are 254 shades of grey from the lightest to the darkest. The normal is an image with pixels of various shades of grey, from the lightest (tending to white) to the darkest (tending to black).

Question 10) From this information mark T (true) or F (false) for each of the following sentences:

( ) From variations of grey tone obtained in satellite images, scientists identify regions of fires and of deforestation.
( ) The presence of clouds does not hinder the detection of fires and of deforestation.
( ) A burnt area, after the fire is extinguished, will reflect more solar radiation than before, when there was vegetation cover, and for this reason, will be represented by light "pixels".
( ) The higher the temperature of the area being burnt, the lighter the pixels that represent the image of that area will be.
( ) Many pixels of an image from a satellite camera intended for monitoring fires have numerical values close to 255. This means the detection of a fire.
problems.problem_orig:
De uma maneira simplificada um satélite de sensoriamento remoto pode ser entendido como uma “máquina fotográfica” que, do espaço, obtém imagens da Terra. A partir dessas imagens é possível monitorar e medir vários fenômenos que ocorrem na superfície terrestre, incluindo queimadas e desmatamento. É importante ressaltar, contudo, que a identificação das queimadas é feita a partir da captação da energia emitida pelo material orgânico em chamas, que ocorre, principalmente na faixa de comprimento de ondas entre 3,7 $\mu$m e 4,1 $\mu$m (1 $\mu$m = $10^{-6}$ m) do espectro eletromagnético, conhecida como termal-média. Sabe-se que quanto maior a temperatura da chama, maior é a emissão de energia. O desmatamento, por sua vez, é identificado a partir da radiação solar refletida em uma faixa de comprimento de onda entre 0,4 $\mu$m e 3,0 $\mu$m. Ao se analisar a radiação solar refletida pelos tipos de superfície nos diversos comprimentos de onda da radiação solar observa-se que a água (rios, lagos e mares) reflete menos energia solar quando comparada ao solo sem cobertura vegetal e ao solo com cobertura vegetal. Além disso, o solo exposto e a vegetação refletem diferentemente em todos os comprimentos de onda, o que permite sua diferenciação. Por se tratarem de fenômenos físicos distintos (emissão e reflexão) o satélite precisa possuir mais de uma câmera imageadora para monitorar o desmatamento e as queimadas.

De modo similar a uma máquina fotográfica digital, as imagens obtidas pelos sensores de um satélite são transformadas em píxeis. Cada imagem é composta de milhões de píxeis. O pixel é o menor elemento da imagem, ao qual é possível atribuir uma tonalidade, cujo valor numérico varia entre zero e 255. Um pixel com valor zero significa que ele recebeu quase nenhuma radiação proveniente da superfície terrestre, sendo então representado pela cor preta. No outro extremo o valor 255 corresponde à cor branca e indica que o sensor recebeu a máxima quantidade de radiação da superfície terrestre. Entre zero e 255 há 254 tons de cinza do mais claro ao mais escuro. O normal é uma imagem com píxeis de diversas tonalidades de cinza, da mais clara (tendendo ao branco) à mais escura (tendendo ao negro).

Pergunta 10) A partir dessas informações assinale V (verdadeira) ou F (falsa) em cada uma das seguintes sentenças:

( ) A partir de variações de tonalidade de cinza obtidas nas imagens dos satélites, os cientistas identificam regiões de queimadas e de desmatamento.
( ) A presença de nuvens não atrapalha a detecção de queimadas e de desmatamento.
( ) Uma área queimada, depois do fogo extinto, irá refletir mais radiação solar do que antes, quando havia cobertura vegetal, e por isso, será representada por “píxeis” claros.
( ) Quanto maior a temperatura da área sendo queimada, mais claros serão os píxeis que representam a imagem dessa área.
( ) Muitos píxeis de uma imagem de uma câmera satelital, destinada ao monitoramento de queimadas, apresentam valores numéricos próximos de 255. Isso significa a detecção de uma queimada.

problems.problem:
There are some methods to identify extrasolar planets, all with their limitations, of course. One of them is the detection of the variation of the radial velocity of the star, due to the presence of a planet around it. That is, when the plane of the orbit of the extrasolar planet is along the line of sight from the Earth, the star alternately approaches and recedes from us. This oscillation can be observed in its spectrum and from it the mass of the planet that this star has can be determined. This oscillation occurs because both (star and planet) revolve around the centre of mass (CM) or barycentre of the system. In the figure beside we represent the star 51 Pegasi, in the constellation of Pegasus, of apparent magnitude 5.5, at a distance of 51 light-years, of mass $M = 2.2\times10^{30}$ kg and its orbit, almost circular (dashed line), and its planet called 51 Pegasi b, with orbital period 4.2 days, of mass $m = 9.5\times10^{26}$ kg and its orbit (also almost circular). Note that: $M = 2316\,m$. The centres of mass of the star and of the planet are separated, on average, by the distance $d = 8\times10^{6}$ km.

4a) (0.5 point) What is the distance from the centre of 51 Pegasi to the barycentre of the system? Let us help. You know that when you are on a seesaw and on the other side there is someone heavier than you, that person needs to stay closer to the centre of the seesaw and you farther from its centre, if you wish, for example, to keep the seesaw still with both balanced horizontally. There is an equation relating their masses ($m_a$ and $m_b$) and respective distances ($r_a$ and $r_b$) to the centre of the seesaw for it to be in equilibrium: $m_a r_a = m_b r_b$. Do you understand now? Just put the star and the planet on the seesaw. Answer 4a): ........ km

4b) (0.25 point) The orbital period of 51 Pegasi b is 4.2 days. What is the orbital period of 51 Pegasi? Note: no calculation is needed. Answer 4b): ........ days

4c) (0.25 point) Make an X on the dashed circle where 51 Pegasi will be when 51 Pegasi b is at the position X indicated in the figure above. Note: of course no calculation is needed either.

Um deles é o da detecção da variação da velocidade radial da estrela, devido à presença de um planeta ao seu redor. Ou seja, quando o plano da órbita do planeta extrassolar está na direção da linha de visada da Terra, a estrela ora se aproxima e ora se afasta de nós. Esta oscilação pode ser observada no seu espectro e com isso pode-se determinar a massa do planeta que esta estrela possui. Esta oscilação ocorre porque ambos (estrela e planeta) giram em torno do centro de massa (CM) ou baricentro do sistema. Na figura ao lado representamos a estrela 51 Pegasi, da constelação de Pégaso, de magnitude aparente 5,5, distante 51 anos-luz, de massa $M = 2{,}2\times10^{30}$ kg e sua órbita, quase circular (linha tracejada) e seu planeta chamado 51 Pegasi b, com período orbital de 4,2 dias, de massa $m = 9{,}5\times10^{26}$ kg e sua órbita (também quase circular). problems.problem:
Another method used to detect extrasolar planets is known as the planetary transit method. Since stars are much larger than planets and emit light, the brightness of the star is slightly reduced by the blocking that the disc of the planet causes during its transit, as the figure beside illustrates (brightness versus time). About 75% of the extrasolar planets discovered so far (about 3600) were found by this method. In February 2017 the discovery, by the transit method, of the extrasolar planetary system TRAPPIST-1 was announced, with seven terrestrial-type planets around it, 4 of them of size similar to the Earth and three of them within the so-called habitable zone. All planets, including the extrasolar ones, must obey Kepler's third law, which is given by:

$$\frac{T^2}{D^3}=\frac{4\pi^2}{G(M+m)}=K$$

where $T$ is the period of the planet, $D$ its mean distance to the star, $M$ the mass of the star, $m$ the mass of the planet, $\pi\cong 3.14$, $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}\ \text{kg}^{-1}\,\text{m}^3\,\text{s}^{-2}$ and $K$ is the Kepler constant.

5a) (0.5 point) Calling $K_S$ the constant for the Solar System and $K_T$ that for the Trappist-1 System, calculate the ratio between $K_S$ and $K_T$, that is, calculate $\dfrac{K_S}{K_T}$.
Data: The orbital period of the Earth ($T$) is 360 days (to simplify the calculations) and its mean distance to the Sun ($D$) is 1 AU (Astronomical Unit). The orbital period of planet "d" ($T_d$) of Trappist-1 is 4 days and its mean distance to Trappist-1 ($D_d$) is 0.02 AU. Since stars have much more mass than planets, neglect $m$ in Kepler's law. Use $M_S$ for the mass of the Sun and $M_T$ for the mass of Trappist-1.

5b) (0.5 point) Calculate how many times the mass of the star Trappist-1, $M_T$, is smaller than that of the Sun, $M_S$, that is, find $\dfrac{M_T}{M_S}$.

onde $T$ é o período do planeta, $D$ sua distância média à estrela, $M$ a massa da estrela, $m$ a massa do planeta, $\pi\cong 3{,}14$, $G = 6{,}67\times10^{-11}\ \text{kg}^{-1}\,\text{m}^3\,\text{s}^{-2}$ e $K$ é a constante de Kepler.

In 2017 the Geostationary Defence and Strategic Communications Satellite (SGDC) was launched. The SGDC was contracted by the Government of Brazil from Visiona Tecnologia Espacial, a national company located in São José dos Campos, SP. The SGDC is located in the equatorial plane of the Earth, 35800 km from its surface. At this great distance it revolves around the Earth with the same angular speed with which the Earth rotates about its axis. Therefore, everything happens as if the SGDC were at rest relative to a fixed point on the Earth's surface. The SGDC is "parked" at 75$^\circ$ West longitude.

Although TV transmission is the main application of geostationary satellites, new technologies allow their use for the transmission of Internet signals, which require, among other things, more power compared with TV. To receive and send signals (electromagnetic waves) the SGDC is equipped with several antennas, some operating in the X band (from 7 to 8 GHz, Giga Hertz = $10^9$ Hz) and several in the Ka band (from 17 to 30 GHz). While the X band is used for military communications (telephony, data, voice and image) the Ka band is used for the Internet.

Instead of using a single "beam" (Figure A), the SGDC projects 67 beams in the Ka band, of about 500 km diameter each. To simplify, only some of these beams are shown in Figure B. In this way, the power of the signal received by each of these regions is much higher than that which would be received if the satellite transmitted using a single beam. It is exactly this multiple-beam technology that allows the use of the SGDC for Internet transmission. On the ground there will be large antennas pointed at the satellites. They are called Gateways, represented by small black circles in Figure B, in beams 15, 24, 33, 36 and 44.

Question 9) (0.2 for each correct answer) Based on this information write C (Correct) or E (Wrong) for each of the statements below:

( ) The same satellite can carry out transmission of data, voice, images and Internet.
( ) The island of Fernando de Noronha is not in the coverage area of the SGDC.
( ) A Brazilian vessel in the Atlantic, outside the Ka-band coverage region of the SGDC satellite, can enjoy the broadband data connection provided by this satellite.
( ) Supposing that the data transmission rate of the SGDC to a certain user is 5 Mbps (Megabit per second), the download of a 50 MB file (MB $\rightarrow$ MegaByte = $10^6$ Byte, with 1 Byte = 8 bits) will take 10 seconds.
( ) Beams 41, 42, 36, 32, 37, 27, 23 and 18 have part or all of their coverage area over the sea. Thus, vessels and oil platforms located in these areas can use the SGDC for Internet connection.

problems.problem:
The light bulbs in homes have printed on them their respective Powers, for example 60 Watt, 100 Watt etc., which defines their "luminosity". Watt, W, is the unit of Power and represents the amount of energy emitted per unit time, that is: Power (W) = Energy (J)/time (s). Stars are big light bulbs, but we call their Power Luminosity ($L$), that is: Luminosity (W) = Energy (J)/time (s). The Power of a light bulb is always the same, no matter whether we are near or far from it. Luminosity is also a property of the star. It also does not depend on whether we are near or far from it. The Power of a light bulb depends on the resistance, current and potential difference. The Luminosity ($L$) of a star depends on the Temperature ($T$) of its surface (measured in Kelvin) and on the area of this surface, that is, on the Radius ($R$) of the star, in the following way:

$$L = k\,(4\pi R^2)\,T^4$$

where $k$ is called the Stefan-Boltzmann constant and equals $k = 5.67\times10^{-8}\ \text{W}\,\text{m}^{-2}\,\text{K}^{-4}$.

Question 3) Calculate the exact value of the Luminosity of the Sun in Watt. Data: Radius of the Sun: about 700000 km. Surface temperature of the Sun: about 6000 K. Ask for more paper if you need more space for the calculations, but attach everything to the paper. Answer 3): ........ W

problems.problem:
The Luminosity of a star is its Power ($P$), that is, the energy (J) that it emits per second (s). Luminosity is measured in Watt (W), just like Power. A 100 Watt light bulb shines a lot if it is near, but little if it is far, because its energy (light) spreads out through all of space and so, the farther away, the less light (energy) we receive from it. The same happens with stars: the farther away we are, the less energy we receive on one square metre, for example. The figure on the right shows that the Luminosity of the Sun, $L_\odot$, is the same that passes through the imaginary spherical surfaces of radii $d$ or $2d$, but, obviously, the "density" of this Luminosity becomes diluted as we move away from the Sun. This "density" is called Flux ($F$), its unit is Watt/metre$^2$ (W/m$^2$) and it is calculated by the expression:

$$F=\frac{L}{4\pi d^2}$$

where $L$ is the luminosity of the star and $d$ the distance from it to us.

problems.problem:
Blue Moon. As the Moon travels around the Earth, over the month, it goes through a cycle of phases. The complete cycle lasts approximately 29.5 days and is called a Lunation. But we have months with 28, 29, 30 and 31 days, so it can happen that in the same month we have two Full Moons. Obviously this is a rare phenomenon. It is even rarer to have two occurrences of this in the same year, as happened in 2018. A rare event, in the folklore of some countries it is called a Blue Moon. Obviously the Moon does not turn blue, except when there are great volcanic eruptions on the Earth, whose particles suspended in the atmosphere scatter the red and then the Moon becomes slightly bluish in any phase.

Blood Moon. On 31/01/18 there was a total eclipse of the Moon and the press made much use of the term "Blood Moon". An extremely inappropriate term, obviously. In every total lunar eclipse the Moon passes through the cone of shadow cast by the Earth, but despite being in the "shadow" it does not become dark or invisible. The incident solar light on the Earth's atmosphere is almost totally scattered, mainly the blue, which is why we see the sky blue. Red light, having a longer wavelength, is less scattered by our atmosphere and, in fact, passes through it and is refracted into the shadow cone. When it reaches the Moon, it is reflected and we see the Moon reddish. Hence associating the reddish colour with blood on the lunar surface is in extremely bad taste.

Super-Moon. The Moon describes around the Earth an elliptical orbit, of low eccentricity, as the figure beside illustrates in an extremely exaggerated way (the figure shows the Earth at the centre of a flattened ellipse labelled "exaggeratedly flattened lunar orbit", with "Moon at perigee" on the left and "Moon at apogee" on the right). When the Full Moon occurs and it is at perigee (or close to it) its diameter can be up to 14% larger than at apogee and up to 30% brighter. Mas temos meses com 28, 29, 30 e 31 dias, logo, pode ocorrer que num mesmo mês tenhamos duas Luas cheias. Obviamente isso é um fenômeno raro. É ainda mais raro termos duas ocorrências destas num mesmo ano, como aconteceu em 2018. Evento raro, no folclore de alguns países é chamado de Lua azul. Obviamente a Lua não fica azul, exceto quando há grandes erupções vulcânicas na Terra, cujas partículas em suspensão na atmosfera espalham o vermelho e, então, a Lua fica ligeiramente azulada em qualquer fase.

Lua de sangue. Em 31/01/18 houve um eclipse total da Lua e a imprensa se utilizou muito do termo "Lua de sangue". Um termo extremamente inadequado, obviamente. Em todo eclipse lunar total a Lua passa pelo cone de sombra projetado pela Terra, mas apesar de estar na "sombra" ela não fica escura ou invisível. A luz solar incidente sobre a atmosfera terrestre é quase totalmente espalhada, principalmente o azul, tanto é que vemos o céu azul. A luz vermelha, por ter comprimento de onda maior, é menos espalhada pela nossa atmosfera e, de fato, a atravessa e sofre refração indo sobre o cone de sombra. Quando atinge a Lua, é refletida e vemos a Lua avermelhada. Daí associar a cor avermelhada a sangue na superfície lunar é de extremo mau gosto.

Super-Lua. A Lua descreve ao redor da Terra uma órbita elíptica, de baixa excentricidade, conforme ilustra de forma extremamente exagerada a figura ao lado (a figura mostra a Terra no centro de uma elipse achatada rotulada "Órbita lunar exageradamente achatada", com "Lua no perigeu" à esquerda e "Lua no apogeu" à direita).
